text: The 'bloat objection' to the extended mind thesis holds that:
choices: External memory devices take up too much physical space to be practical
The functional criterion is too permissive, threatening to fold an unmanageable range of environmental resources into the cognitive system
Notebooks and other aids store too much redundant information to be reliable
The brain becomes metabolically overloaded when it depends on external tools
explanation: The bloat objection (associated with Adams and Aizawa) says that counting anything playing a cognitive functional role as part of the mind would swell cognition to include books, the internet, even the built environment. Clark and Chalmers reply that their three conditions restrict membership; critics counter that the conditions remain too permissive and conflate resources a system uses with resources that constitute it. It is not about physical space, redundancy, or metabolism.
